title: Bitcoin / BTC (The Sovereign Store)
function: The original decentralized digital asset operating as peer-to-peer electronic cash without a central clearinghouse.
rule: Enforces a hardcapped supply limit of exactly 21,000,000 coins embedded directly into its source code, utilizing a programmed supply tightening event (Halving) every 210,000 blocks.
technicalNote: Bitcoin's consensus halving interval is 210,000 blocks. The theoretical issuance limit is approximately 21 million BTC, and halvings are block-triggered, not fixed-calendar events.

title: Ethereum / ETH (The Programmable State Machine)
function: A global, decentralized computing platform that executes self-contained logic agreements known as smart contracts.
rule: Utilizes a native Turing-complete virtual machine (EVM) to process decentralized applications, burning a portion of transaction costs (Base Fee) to structurally manage asset supply based on network demand.

title: Solana / SOL (The High-Velocity Monolith)
function: A high-throughput layer-1 blockchain engineered for speed, sub-second settlement times, and ultra-low transaction overhead.
rule: Chains events together using a specialized cryptographic clock, allowing nodes to process transactions concurrently without waiting for a global block validation cycle.
technicalNote: Proof of History is a verifiable ordering/clock mechanism used with Solana's stake-weighted Tower BFT consensus. Block production is not the same as irreversible transaction finality.

title: XRP / Ripple Ledger (The Institutional Settlement Hub)
function: A specialized digital asset and independent open-source ledger optimized for instant cross-border fiat currency settlement.
rule: Replaces traditional miners with a unique federated consensus mechanism where trusted validator nodes quickly agree on network updates every few seconds, eliminating heavy computing costs.
technicalNote: The XRP Ledger is independent of Ripple the company; each server relies on its own configured list of trusted validators for consensus. XRP transactions do not themselves guarantee fiat payout.

title: BNB / Build and Build (The Ecosystem Fuel)
function: The native utility token powering the BNB Chain ecosystem, decentralized finance applications, and high-volume asset exchanges.
rule: Executes a systematic quarterly coin destruction schedule based on trading volume and transaction metrics, permanently shrinking supply until exactly 100,000,000 tokens remain in circulation.
technicalNote: BNB Auto-Burn is reported quarterly and calculated using BNB price plus BSC block production, not exchange trading volume. A separate BEP-95 mechanism burns part of gas fees.

title: Chainlink / LINK (The Cryptographic Oracle)
function: A decentralized oracle network that securely feeds real-world external data points directly into isolated blockchain smart contracts.
rule: Enforces a strict reputation and collateral system where data providers must stake native tokens to verify the authenticity of their inputs before they are delivered to a blockchain.
technicalNote: Chainlink staking is available for particular services and eligible participants; not every data provider must stake LINK. In v0.2 slashing covers specified node operator stakers.

title: Monero / XMR (The Absolute Anonymity Vector)
function: A privacy-focused open-source cryptocurrency engineered to ensure completely untraceable transaction histories.
rule: Obfuscates sending addresses, receiving addresses, and specific asset transfer volumes by default using advanced cryptography, making it impossible to audit individual ledger balances externally.
technicalNote: Monero provides strong default on-chain privacy through ring signatures, stealth addresses and RingCT, not an unconditional guarantee of perfect anonymity. Wallet disclosures, networks and other off-chain information can reveal activity.

title: ASIC Mining / Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (The Industrial Standard)
function: Deploying highly specialized, hardcoded microchips custom-built for the sole purpose of solving a specific hashing algorithm (like Bitcoin's SHA-256).
rule: Maximizes raw mathematical guessing frequency (terahashes per second) while discarding all non-essential operating system code to achieve maximum power efficiency.

title: GPU Mining / Graphics Processing Unit (The Adaptable Array)
function: Utilizing consumer graphics card processing arrays to mine memory-intensive altcoin cryptographic proof-of-work algorithms.
rule: Leverages high-bandwidth video memory to process complex memory routing tasks, allowing miners to switch between different asset algorithms via minor software changes.

title: CPU Mining / Central Processing Unit (The Desktop Invariant)
function: Harnessing the general-purpose processing cores of standard consumer computers to secure lightweight or specialized privacy networks.
rule: Operates on strict memory-hard algorithms specifically designed to neutralize the raw calculation speed of high-powered ASICs, preserving network accessibility for standard personal computers.
technicalNote: CPU/ASIC resistance depends on the chosen proof-of-work algorithm and evolves as implementations and hardware improve; CPU mining is not intrinsically ASIC-proof.

title: FPGA Mining / Field-Programmable Gate Array (The Hybrid Bridge)
function: Using reprogrammable integrated circuits that can be reconfigured at the hardware level to mine shifting altcoin algorithms.
rule: Bridges the gap between general GPUs and rigid ASICs, allowing operators to flash entirely new logic pathways onto the physical chip to follow volatile mining trends.

title: Cloud Mining (The Remote Allocation Contract)
function: Acquiring computational mining power from distant, industrial-scale data centers through a rented hash-rate contract.
rule: The user pays an upfront fiat or digital asset fee to lease a specific block of processing power, completely offloading physical hardware maintenance, heat dissipation, and local energy costs to the facility provider.
technicalNote: Cloud mining contracts introduce counterparty, non-delivery, fee, and fraud risks; paying for a contract does not guarantee mined rewards. This module offers no contract purchasing.

title: Solo Mining (The High-Risk Jackpot)
function: A singular independent mining rig or facility attempting to solve and publish a valid block directly to the public ledger entirely on its own.
rule: The operator receives 100% of the newly minted block rewards and network fees if they solve the puzzle, but faces massive income volatility since finding a block depends entirely on their percentage of total global hash power.
technicalNote: Solo miners receive the applicable block subsidy plus included transaction fees if successful, net of applicable costs. Block-finding probability depends on relative hash rate and protocol difficulty; payout rules vary by mining setup.

title: Pool Mining (The Structured Cooperative)
function: Thousands of individual mining rigs combining their computational processing power over a network to solve blocks cooperatively.
rule: The central pool operator coordinates the global mining effort and distributes block rewards proportionally to all participants based on the specific amount of computational work each rig contributes.
technicalNote: Pools divide rewards according to specific pool rules (e.g., PPS or PPLNS), fees and share accounting; not always simple proportional allocation.

title: Proof of Work / PoW (The Thermodynamic Anchor)
function: The foundational consensus mechanism where nodes spend immense electrical and physical computational energy to secure the ledger.
rule: Forces computers to continuously guess a cryptographic puzzle until a valid solution is discovered, anchoring digital security directly to real-world energy expenditures to prevent ledger manipulation.

title: Proof of Stake / PoS (The Capital Allocation Model)
function: A consensus framework where block validation duties are granted based on the specific amount of native tokens a user locks up as collateral.
rule: Eliminates heavy hardware energy costs by replacing miners with validators, automatically seizing or burning a user's staked assets (Slashing) if they approve malicious or fraudulent transactions.
technicalNote: PoS design differs by network. On Ethereum, slashing applies to specific provable validator offenses, while offline/late validation ordinarily receives other penalties.

title: Proof of History / PoH (The Temporal Sequencing Layer)
function: A specialized pre-consensus mechanism that builds a reliable, unalterable historical log of time directly into the data stream.
rule: Runs a continuous cryptographic hashing loop that proves an event occurred at a precise point in time, allowing the network to process transactions instantly without needing nodes to constantly coordinate timestamps.
technicalNote: PoH supplies verifiable event ordering and elapsed-work evidence rather than absolute wall-clock timestamps or instant finality; it does not replace Tower BFT consensus.

title: Proof of Authority / PoA (The Identity Registry)
function: A highly centralized, high-velocity consensus model engineered for private enterprise blockchains and localized test networks.
rule: Grants explicit block creation and validation privileges exclusively to a small pool of pre-approved, highly vetted server nodes whose real-world identities act as their operational collateral.
technicalNote: PoA is permissioned by design, but not all deployments have the same centralization, identity disclosure, governance or latency characteristics.

title: Liquid Staking Architecture (The Capital Unlocking Bridge)
function: A decentralized financial design that allows users to stake assets to secure a network while preserving their liquidity.
rule: When a user locks up their native tokens in a staking pool, the platform mints an equivalent, freely tradable wrapper token that tracks the underlying value, allowing them to participate in other financial markets simultaneously.
technicalNote: Liquid-staking tokens are not guaranteed to trade at exactly the underlying asset price. They add smart-contract, validator, redemption, depegging and liquidity risks.

title: Layer 2 Rollups / Optimistic & ZK (The Execution Offloader)
function: Secondary network infrastructures built on top of a primary layer-1 blockchain to handle thousands of transactions off-chain.
rule: Bundles hundreds of separate transfers into a single compressed data packet and posts it back to the main ledger, radically cutting user network fees while inheriting the base layer's ultimate security.
technicalNote: Optimistic and ZK rollups differ in dispute/proof models, withdrawal times, and data availability; inherited L1 security is conditional on the design, not automatic for every L2.

title: Halving Mechanics (The Programmed Scarcity Clock)
function: The automated deflationary mechanism built directly into core proof-of-work protocols to systematically control asset inflation.
rule: Slashes the exact block generation reward issued to miners precisely in half at fixed block milestones, structurally forcing down the supply of new coins entering the market over time.
technicalNote: Halving is a property of certain issuance schedules, not a rule for all proof-of-work networks. Bitcoin reduces its subsidy at every 210,000-block milestone.
